skill.name: design-to-production
skill.description: Guided workflow for converting HTML design prototypes into production React components with glassmorphism styling, shadcn/ui mapping, scaffolding, and validation.
skill.summary: Convert glassmorphism HTML prototypes into validated React TypeScript components.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, documented .claude paths, fixed shell path calculations, and UI validation text. The real risks are unvalidated local paths in helper scripts that can read files or write generated components outside intended project areas. I found no prompt injection, network access, credential harvesting, or malicious exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Scaffold paths are built from unvalidated component and module arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict module names to known module slugs and component names to TypeScript identifiers. Resolve the final path and reject anything outside frontend/src/modules.

remediation.issue: Extractor and validator scripts accept broad file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute paths and .. segments. Use realpath and require prototypes under .superdesign/design_iterations and components under frontend/src.

remediation.issue: Generated JSON and source output are assembled with shell text substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Use a JSON-safe writer such as jq for structure output and escape template replacement values before sed interpolation.

remediation.issue: Local Bash helpers can create or inspect files during the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Document exactly which paths are read or written and ask for confirmation before overwriting existing component files.

| `layout-section` | Page sections, containers | Layout wrapper, grid/flex patterns |

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Scaffold Output Path
semantic_findings.description: The scaffolding script accepts component and module names from command arguments and uses them to build the generated file path. Without identifier and path boundary checks, a crafted value could write outside the intended module tree or overwrite an unexpected file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command-line values are copied into MODULE_PATH, COMPONENT_PATH, and OUTPUT_FILE before the template is written. The script does not restrict names to safe identifiers or verify the final path remains under the expected directory.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Prototype File Read
semantic_findings.description: The structure extraction script accepts an HTML file path and reads it through a project-root-prefixed path. It does not reject absolute paths or traversal segments before running grep over the selected file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly uses the provided path in existence checks and grep commands. The impact is limited because output is local and summarized, but boundary checks are missing.

semantic_findings.title: Validation Script Arbitrary File Read Fallback
semantic_findings.description: The validation script falls back to reading the supplied component path directly when it exists outside the expected frontend source path. It then runs line counts and grep checks over that file and can print matching content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback to FULL_PATH="$COMPONENT_PATH" is explicit, and later checks read that file. No network or secret collection behavior was found, so this is a local file boundary issue.

content.user_title: Convert HTML Prototypes to React Components
content.value_statement: Design prototypes often take too long to rebuild by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through analysis, scaffolding, and validation for React components.
actual_capabilities: Extracts structure from HTML prototypes with a provided shell script.
Maps HTML elements to shadcn/ui and shared UI components.
Scaffolds React TypeScript components from three templates.
Preserves approved glassmorphism utility classes in className output.
Validates file size, interface naming, any types, classes, and import patterns.
Provides reference guides for common layout and component patterns.
limitations: Designed for projects matching the DevPrep AI frontend structure.
Requires local Bash scripts and write access to target component folders.
Does not fully implement business logic; generated files contain TODOs.
Best suited for glassmorphism prototypes, not arbitrary design systems.

use_cases.title: Implement a Finished Prototype
use_cases.description: Convert an approved HTML prototype into a typed React component with consistent structure and styling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Decisions
use_cases.description: Map repeated buttons, cards, inputs, badges, and layouts to approved shadcn/ui patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Generated UI Quality
use_cases.description: Run local validation checks for line count, interface names, any usage, classes, and imports.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Simple Prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this HTML prototype into a React component using the design-to-production workflow. Use the default mapping unless a decision needs my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Map Components Before Coding
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this prototype and list the component name, target module, shadcn/ui mappings, props, and glassmorphism classes before scaffolding.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold and Validate a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold a React TypeScript component for this prototype, preserve approved glassmorphism classes, then run the validation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Complex Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this complex prototype into production components. Split repeated sections, choose templates, define props, and explain any manual logic left for me.

output_examples.input: A hints panel HTML prototype with glass cards and reveal buttons.
output: A recommended component name and module placement.
A mapped set of Button, Card, and Alert choices.
A scaffolded React component plan with TODOs for reveal logic.
A validation summary covering size, types, classes, and imports.

output_examples.input: A landing page stats section using glassmorphism cards and a grid.
output: A reusable stat card structure with typed props.
Approved class names for cards, gradient text, and responsive grid layout.

output_examples.input: An existing component that was generated from a prototype.
output: A quality check report for line count, interface naming, any types, glass classes, and import patterns.
Suggested fixes for invalid classes or project import style issues.

best_practices: Start with a finalized HTML prototype and a known target module.
Review component mapping decisions before running scaffold generation.
Run validation after implementation and address warnings before review.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for early exploratory designs that still change often.
Scaffolding into unknown modules without checking project structure first.
Accepting generated TODOs as finished production business logic.

faq.question: Does this skill write production-ready components automatically?
faq.answer: It creates a strong component shell, but developers still complete business logic, state, and final review.

faq.question: Which project structure does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a frontend source tree with modules, shared UI imports, and local glassmorphism styles.

faq.question: Can I use it without glassmorphism styles?
faq.answer: You can adapt parts of the workflow, but the references and validation rules target glassmorphism classes.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What files can it generate?
faq.answer: The scaffolder generates React TypeScript component files from interactive card, display card, and layout section templates.

faq.question: What should I check before running scripts?
faq.answer: Confirm that file paths stay inside your project and that the target component path is safe to create or overwrite.
